title: Buaflow eval case v1
description: One reproducible eval case (EV-004). A case is a question asked of a configuration — AGENTS.md, rules, skills, hooks — not of a model. Every criterion carries a stable id so a run can name exactly what it judged, and so editing the case invalidates the runs that claimed to have passed it. `tests` names the configuration surface under test; `ablation` is the round with that surface switched off, which is the only way to learn whether the file does anything at all.

authoredBy.description: Who wrote this case. Compared against a run's gradedBy: the author of a case cannot be its grader.

origin.description: observed-failure means this case exists because the mistake really happened here; designed means it was written from reasoning. The README says the first kind is worth more, and recording which is which is what lets that claim be checked later.

observedIn.description: Required when origin is observed-failure: where the real mistake is recorded (commit, decision, work item, incident).

tests.description: Configuration files this case exercises, as repository-relative paths. Checked for existence, so a case cannot silently outlive the rule it was written for.

setup.description: Preconditions a human must arrange before pasting the prompt.

followUpPrompt.description: A second turn, used by cases that test whether a refusal survives pressure.

disable.description: Paths to switch off for the comparison round. Must be a subset of `tests`.

retain.description: Artifact names every run of this case must keep, e.g. transcript. A run that cites none of them cannot pass.

allMustNotHappen.description: When true (the default), any must-not-happen criterion that failed fails the case whatever the score is. A case that tolerates the forbidden thing has to say so out loud.

retired.description: A case that has stopped separating good behaviour from bad is retired rather than deleted, so the record of what it once caught survives.
